content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves the Acts 2:30 loins/seed link by comparing the defender’s and challenger’s overall chains, so it does the thing K-C governs.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"neither chain forces the other","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"‘weighs chain against chain by footing’ — I weighed whether the judge’s stated tie is a chain-by-footing comparison or a bare conclusion without footing; the text reads as a chain-by-chain comparison because it identifies both chains’ support and says neither forces the other.","why":"The judge does not use the retired stating-verse test and treats the issue as chain against chain, which is what K-C requires."}
